name: Red Wool Bandana
summary: In the Stormwind Stockade, Red Wool Bandana scraps mark the Defias Brotherhood. Prisoners tear wool from their blankets and wear the red cloth as emblems of defiance.

sections.title: Stitched in Defiance
sections.body: In the Stormwind Stockade, Defias Brotherhood inmates keep their identity alive. They secretly tear scraps from prison wool blankets and stitch them into red bandanas. Guards treat the scarves as contraband, and finding them can spark fatal mutinies. Each bandana declares that the brotherhood and its rebellion endure, even in chains.

sections.title: A Grandmother's Vengeance
sections.body: Red Wool Bandanas are tied to the death of Mac Raskol, a fourteen-year-old prison guard. He caught inmates shredding blankets for scarves and tried to discipline them. Defias convicts stabbed him in the back. His grieving grandmother, Nikova, now seeks adventurers to enter the rioting dungeon, cull the rioters, and bring back a crimson cloth as proof of vengeance.

faq.q: Where do prisoners get these bandanas in the Stockade?
aliases: how do they make red bandanas
faq.answer: Defias inmates tear the bandanas from their prison-issue wool blankets. Though disarmed and imprisoned, they turn their meager bedding into signs of defiance to wear in their cells.

Nikova Raskol, a grieving grandmother in Stormwind, asks adventurers to collect the bandanas. Her fourteen-year-old grandson Mac guarded the Stockade, and prisoners murdered him after he caught them making the scarves.

faq.q: Why do the prisoners care so much about wearing red scarves?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood wears red masks and bandanas as its gang colors and uniform. Behind bars, the scraps help inmates keep their rank, morale, and unity.
Almost any rioting Defias member in the Stockade carries one, including Defias Captives, Inmates, Prisoners, Insurgents, and Convicts.

angles.text: For Alliance defenders, recovering these bandanas brings grim justice for young Mac Raskol and strikes at the rioters holding the city's prison.
These rough bandanas show how desperate hands in captivity can unravel coarse wool blankets and put the fibers to use again.
